note: rebuild Oct 29: hook re-cut and 75 s cap (IMPROVE 00a, 00c), fresh opus reviewer
reasons: 1. As an HVAC owner, here's what it tells me: homeowners lean hard on reviews and a lot of contractors don't answer them, so here are a five-star reply and a one-star reply to copy. Answer the bad ones short and calm, take it offline, and spend ten minutes on reviews every Monday.

2. Stop: yes. The 0.8 s frame is a phone close-up with 'Got a 1-star review?', a 1-star card that says 'The tech showed up late.' and 'Copy this reply.' in the reply box. Every owner has had that review. The voice line 'Got a one-star review? Here's your reply to copy.' matches the screen and promises a concrete payoff, so it doesn't read as a tease.

3. Save: yes. Both replies are short enough to paste straight into Google, and the caption gives fill-in templates ([job], [fell short]). Send: yes. The close names a real person to send it to (whoever runs your Google profile) and gives a reason (so the next one-star gets a reply). Follow or link: yes, a soft check. The only ask is 'Free tools for trade owners: link in bio' in the caption, and there's no pitch in the video.

4. No hype, no fake urgency, no pitch, and it doesn't feel like AI slop. 'One honest note... It doesn't prove a reply wins the job' (0:52.8 to 1:00.1) is what earns my trust. The AI voice is disclosed (aiLabel true). Nothing here would make me scroll past.

4b. Earlier faults stay fixed. The preachy 'Don't be one' line is gone, and the close is now 'Don't leave reviews hanging.' (1:04.3). The caption's 45/43/13 split now carries '(rounded)'. The 43% is now voiced precisely as 'third-party sites'.

5. Minor, not blocking: the one-star reply the hook promises doesn't arrive until 0:37.5. Before it come about 24 s of stats (0:03.7 to 0:27.7) and then the five-star reply first. An impatient viewer could drop in that stretch. Fix for a future cut: give the one-star reply first, or cut the stats to one line before the replies.

5b. Minor, not blocking: 'That's The ACHR News.' (0:10.0) is clipped and means nothing to a stranger by voice alone. Fix: 'That's from The ACHR News, an HVAC trade paper.' (The caption already explains it.)

5c. Minor, not blocking: 'Ninety-one percent of the four hundred homeowners' (0:12.2) says 'the' as if those homeowners were already introduced, but the line before talked about contractors. Fix: 'In the same survey, ninety-one percent of four hundred homeowners...'

5d. Minor, not blocking: 'So if you answer reviews on those sites, you're with the forty-five percent who do.' (0:22.9) lands flat and doesn't tell me why it matters. Fine to keep, but a tighter cut could drop it.
6. Trust: yes. It names the source and the sample size, the caption gives the date (Sept 2024), it admits the data's limit, and the replies sound like something a real shop owner would say.
